target_customer: Premium consumers and homeowners wanting a water saving spa like shower
problem: Showers waste water and energy; Nebia atomizes water to deliver a full experience with far less.
business_model: Hardware product sales with Kickstarter preorders, later retail partners

founders.name: Philip Winter
founders.background_notes: Sold the company to Brondell per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Water atomizing nozzle design and manufacturing at consumer price needed hardware engineering and tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Patented nozzle technology cited by Brondell, but large plumbing brands had competing atomizing showers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Moen partnered and led the 2019 Series A, with a joint Nebia by Moen product in 2020; Brondell bought Nebia in January 2023.

market_need_then: Water conservation concerns, especially in California; a 2015 Kickstarter presold over $10M across six campaigns per YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Design awards (iF listing) and press including Tim Cook as an investor; strong product identity. Name origin not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Nebia used Kickstarter presales and a patented nozzle to reach shipping hardware, added Moen as investor and distribution partner in 2019, and sold to Brondell in January 2023 with its brand kept alive. Price undisclosed; a 15 person team and about $7.18M raised per CB Insights suggest a capital efficient but modest exit.
notes: YC page says acquired in 2022; press release dated 2023-01-26. Round amounts not stated in opened sources; CB Insights total $7.18M is aggregator only. Hansgrohe Powder Rain and Delta H2OKinetic appear only in Nebia's own undated comparison, so not recorded as 2015 competitors. nebia.com redirects to brondell.com; Brondell page not fetched.
